headline: Bayern without Musiala at third-placed Freiburg — still clear favourites
summary: Bayern go to third-placed Freiburg on Sunday without Jamal Musiala, who Sky report is not yet back in team training. Freiburg's unbeaten start ended on 18 October, 1-2 at Bayer Leverkusen, while Bayern's last league game was a 6-1 win over Leipzig. Wednesday brought a 2-2 at Arsenal, so Bayern have 4 days between games and Freiburg a full week. Even so, the market has Bayern 69.3% favourites to Freiburg's 14.7%, gives Freiburg a head start of 1.5 goals, and expects a high-scoring game although the fair total eased from 4.0 to 3.9.
read: Bayern are unbeaten and top of the Bundesliga, and the market makes them 69.3% favourites at third-placed Freiburg, rated about a goal and a half the better side. Freiburg have had a full week to prepare while Bayern come off a 2-2 with Arsenal and are without Jamal Musiala, and the goals line sits at four with the money edging slightly towards fewer goals.

facts.fact: Bayern are 69.3% to win at Freiburg, more than four times Freiburg's 14.7%.
facts.meaning: The market sees a clear away win, not a close game between first and third.

facts.fact: Bayern lead the Bundesliga with 14 points from six games; Freiburg are third on 13.
facts.meaning: Only one point separates them, but Bayern are unbeaten (4 wins, 2 draws) while Freiburg have already lost once.

facts.fact: Sky report that Jamal Musiala will miss the Freiburg match, and at least two more games, because he is not yet back in team training.
facts.meaning: Bayern's main creative midfielder is unavailable for the trip to the side sitting third.

facts.fact: Bayern beat RB Leipzig 6-1 on Matchday six, Luis Díaz scoring a hat-trick and Harry Kane also on the scoresheet.
facts.meaning: The leaders' attacking form is why this game is priced as a high-scoring one rather than a controlled away win.

facts.fact: Bayern drew 2-2 with Arsenal on Wednesday and have four days until Freiburg; Freiburg have had seven days since their last game.
facts.meaning: Bayern arrive off a full Champions League night with a short week; Freiburg have had a full week to prepare.

facts.fact: Freiburg's unbeaten Bundesliga start ended on 18 October with a 1-2 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen.
facts.meaning: Their first loss of the season came against one of the sides above them; Bayern are a step up again.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is 1.49 goals — the market rates Bayern about a goal and a half better than Freiburg.
facts.meaning: Bayern are expected to win, and to win by more than one; Freiburg starting +1.5 is close to a coin flip.

facts.fact: Bayern have averaged 3.63 xG across their last five matches, creating at least 2.5 in every one of them.
facts.meaning: Even in their draws Bayern created heavily, so the goals expectation rests on chance quality and not only on the 6-1 and 7-0 scorelines.

sources.fact: Sky report that Jamal Musiala will miss the Bundesliga top match against SC Freiburg as he is not yet back in team training.
According to Sky, Musiala will also miss at least two further games, including the Freiburg match on Sunday.
Bayern beat RB Leipzig 6-1 on Matchday six, with Luis Díaz scoring a hat-trick and Harry Kane also on the scoresheet, after two consecutive draws.
Bayern drew 2-2 with Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Harry Kane scoring a penalty and Alphonso Davies also on target.
Bayern remain top of the Bundesliga going into the Freiburg match, with Freiburg third.
Freiburg's unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season ended with a defeat at Bayer Leverkusen, Patrik Schick scoring in a fifth straight Leverkusen win.
Freiburg go into the Bayern match third in the table, with Bayern top.
Bundesliga.com reports that Freiburg still have an open score to settle with Bayern and sees a chance of an upset this time.
